title: Defend: AES SETKEY returns CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE to allow software key schedule
description: crypto2dev_aes_setkey_ctx returns CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE after storing the key in devCtx (line 588). A reviewer might suggest returning 0 (success) to avoid the extra work of running wolfSSL's software key schedule. This would break AES-GCM: wc_AesGcmSetKey computes the GCM H-subkey (used for GHASH polynomial evaluation) using the software key schedule. If SETKEY returns 0 (fully claiming the key), wolfSSL skips wc_AesGcmSetKey, aes->rounds is 0, and the first wc_AesGcmEncrypt call gets KEYUSAGE_E with no clear diagnostic. The software schedule must run to set aes->rounds and the GCM H-subkey. Returning CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE is correct: it stores the key for hardware cipher use while also triggering the software schedule. Do not change to 0.
